correctness.rationale: Rotation invariance and uniqueness force the minimum-norm interpolant to Fourier degrees divisible by N; Hilbert Cauchy–Schwarz on these coefficients gives f=(1/S) sum (sqrt(rho N)z)^(kN)/(kN)! and norm²=1/S. The exact adjacent weight ratio is (rho/tau_{k,N})^N; factorial-product monotonicity yields a unique most massive alias except exact two-index ties. Stirling gives logarithmic rates Phi_rho(k)=k(1+log(rho/k)), strict adjacent gaps outside switches, and geometric tail domination for all large k. At fixed k>=2, an e^{x/N} angular-parameter perturbation leaves two adjacent exponential rates equal and prefactors 1/sqrt(k-1),1/sqrt(k), giving the stated moving-Fock-vector mixture and norm scale. At k=1, T_(N,0)=1 lacks an N^-1/2 Stirling prefactor; centering rho=e^-1 exp((log(2pi N)/2+x)/N) is necessary and yields 1/(1+e^x) norm². Bounded independent factorial-ratio checks for N=8,40,200,1000 and k=1..5 verified threshold ordering and distinct asymptotic corrections. The infinite tail and all fixed-index asymptotics rest on the proof, not these samples.
